verdict.headline: Semis led S&P above 7,480 for the first time; oil re-escalated on Iran tanker attack
verdict.label: SPX closes at 7,509 on memory-led chip surge; WTI rises to $84 on Iran strike and Houthi embargo; GOOGL/TSLA binary tonight
verdict.rationale_short: The S&P 500 closed at 7,509, the first close above the 7,480 formal trigger, starting the two-session upgrade clock — but the day's cross-asset read is split. Memory stocks powered the advance: Micron surged 12% after Morgan Stanley forecast 25% memory-price gains, and the semiconductor sector gauge rose 5.2%. AMD reversed a +4% premarket Rosenblatt gap to close -1.4%, entering AMD AI Day from a position of weakness. WTI settled near $84.42 — up $2.13 from morning — after Iran attacked a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi militants declared a maritime embargo against Saudi Arabia, adding roughly 2.5M bbl/day to the supply-disruption risk. GOOGL and TSLA report after Wednesday's close; the outcome sets the regime for the next four weeks.

bear_case: Counter-thesis: The July 21 rally was memory-led short-covering, not broad AI infrastructure confirmation. Micron's 12% surge responded to a Morgan Stanley price forecast, not actual pricing data, while the two most consequential AI stocks — NVDA (+1.4%) and AMD (-1.4%) — significantly underperformed the 5.2% sector gain. AMD's intraday reversal from +4% premarket to a -1.4% close is a direct warning signal: if the market cannot hold a gap on a Rosenblatt Top Pick upgrade with a $175 price-target increase, the bar for AMD AI Day Day 1 to sustain a gap is materially higher. WTI rising to $84.42 on the same session SPX cleared 7,480 is a split signal — equity bulls are pricing in earnings relief while oil markets are pricing in further Hormuz escalation via a new Houthi maritime embargo against Saudi Arabia. A GOOGL Cloud miss on July 22 AMC would immediately test whether the 7,480 SPX break was structural or a one-session short-squeeze overshoot, resetting the upgrade clock to zero and extending the STEP ASIDE regime into a fifth week. Invalidation: if GOOGL Cloud revenue growth exceeds 22% YoY and TSLA gross margin exceeds 15%, the double-beat confirms the July 21 SPX break was structural, not a squeeze.
